title: Uncle Ezra’s Hayloft Jamboree
text: The Weeping Water American Legion Auxiliary will present a home talent show, Uncle Ezra’s Hayloft Jamboree, at the high school auditorium on Thursday and Saturday evenings, March 22 and 24, for the benefit of Girl’s State and for rehabilitation work in veterans hospitals. Uncle Ezra’s Hayloft Jamboree is a fast moving radio type show with the famous Joe Kelly and the Quiz Kids, to be enacted by Slick Johnson and pupils from the local school. LuluBelle and Scotty will be Mary and Neil Fitzpatrick, Uncle Ezry will be Ray Knott, while Hiram Hicks will be Lynn Parson. Square dancers will be Doc and Mary Herman, Mr and Mrs Byron Baker and Mr and Mrs William Newham, who will dance to Walt Patton’s calling. A few of the other entertainers are: Archie Crozier, Verne Malstead, Bonnie Van Every, Chuck Philpot, Toni Lee Lowe, Irene Johnson, Kay Baker, Hap & Betty Otte, Harrison Hartley, Maribello Elliott, Patty Otte, Marcy Nichols, Vicki Porter, a polka band, and a score more of your friends and neighbors from Weeping Water and surrounding communities. Dancing will include the 1951 version of the Charleston, hula, polka, novelty tap and others. Vocal and instrumental numbers will be in keeping with the hayloft atmosphere of the production.

title: Father’s paintings in Ford Times
text: FATHER’S PAINTINGS IN FORD TIMES. Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick was thrilled to find that two of her father’s paintings are in this issue of the Ford Times magazine. They are reproduced in color. Mrs. Fitzpatrick’s father is the artist, Mr. Harrison Hartley, of St. Joseph, Mo.

title: Who’s Who in American Artists
text: WHO’S WHO IN AMERICAN ARTISTS. Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick received word that her father, Harrison Hartley, St. Joseph, Mo., has received recognition by Who’s Who in American Artists, by the inclusion of his name in their national registrar. Hartley works primarily in water color, and his “natural” is landscapes. He also works with oils.

title: Michael as the lame boy
text: The third grade, with their teacher, Mrs Dimmitt, gave the Pied Piper of Hamlin. Narrators were Beverly Finley, Nicky Lane, and Marilyn Schmadeke. David Rutledge as the Pied Piper, Tommy Wipf as Mayor and Michael Fitzpatrick as the lame boy gave realistic performances as did the rats who left town so willingly.

title: Brian as Geppetto
text: [Pinocchio] given by the second grade and Mrs James Kivett, George Friesell as Pinocchio appeared to have stepped off the pages of a book with his lively hopping friend Jiminy Cricket, played by Donald Elliott. Others in the cast were: Narrator, Linda Rasmussen; Geppetto, Brian Fitzpatrick; Figaro, the pet cat, Jimmy Michelsen; blue fairy, Jill Domingo; the wicked fox, Gene Moore; the wicked [cat]…

title: A baby boy, Dennis Frederick
text: Mr. and Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick are parents of a baby boy, Dennis Frederick, born Friday afternoon at St. Mary’s hospital in Nebraska City. Dennis weighed 7 pounds, 2 ounces. Mrs. Fitzpatrick’s parents, Mr. and Mrs. Harrison Hartley, St. Joseph, Mo., came Saturday and Mr. Hartley returned Sunday morning to their home in Missouri. Mrs. Hartley is staying with Brian, Mike and Sheila Fitzpatrick until their mother and brother return home. Other grandparents are Mr. and Mrs. Art Fitzpatrick.

title: “The Answer,” by Mary Fitzpatrick
text: THE ANSWER. By Mary Fitzpatrick. Baby’s hair is a halo golden / Etched against my heart. / Baby’s eyes are young but olden / Taking my soul apart. / Baby’s ears hear angel syllables / Not meant for you and me. / Baby is special, baby is me, / Baby is you at your mother’s knee. / They answer the question of ‘why are we here?’ / When we hold our wonderful baby near. / And when to his baby his love will flow, / He’ll know how we felt, so long ago.

title: “Seventeen,” by Mary Fitzpatrick
text: SEVENTEEN. By Mary Fitzpatrick. He looked my way—I know he did. / Or was it that red head up ahead? / His eyes are green, like new spring grass. / He looks at me all through the class. / He loves me not, he loves me best. / Oh what a strong and manly chest! / He touched my arm, I think I’ll die. / Why couldn’t I like some other guy? / A date? Oh wait now, let me see. / Call tomorrow, Maybe I’m free. / It’s heaven. It’s torture. It’s sheer delight. / How can I stand it ’till Saturday night? / I wish I were 60- or even dead; / But I guess I’ll just have to wait instead.

title: Named Arthur Shawn
text: Mr and Mrs Neil Fitzpatrick are the parents of a baby boy, born Monday, January 19, at 2:00 a.m., at the St. Mary’s Hospital in Nebraska City. The baby has been named Arthur Shawn. The maternal grandparents are Mr and Mrs Harrison Hartley of St. Joseph, Mo. and the paternal grandparents are Mr and Mrs Art Fitzpatrick of Weeping Water.

title: Grandfather takes the children painting
text: Mr and Mrs H. S. Hartley of St. Joseph, Mo., visited Saturday and Sunday with Mr and Mrs Neil Fitzpatrick and family. Mr Hartley sold three of his paintings to George Wiles. On Sunday afternoon, Mr Hartley took his grandchildren, with him to do paintings of the scenery around here.

title: Sheila’s “My Teddy Bear”
text: Painting Chosen For Art Exhibit. Shelia Fitzpatrick, daughter of Mr and Mrs Neil Fitzpatrick, will have a painting “My Teddy Bear” on display at the Nebraska Elementary School Art Exhibit, held at Miller and Paine, April 18 to 25. Shelia’s picture is one of the 474 drawings chosen from the thousands submitted from schools all over Nebraska. This will be the 12th All State Exhibit. Miss Fitzpatrick is a kindergarten pupil of Mrs R. A. Shumaker.

title: Missouri vacation
text: MISSOURI VACATION. Brian and Mike Fitzpatrick went by train to St. Joseph, Mo., where they visited for five days with their grandparents, Mr. and Mrs. H. S. Hartley and with their aunt and uncle, Mr and Mrs L. N. Fortner. They returned home last Monday.

title: Designs Pony Express pamphlet
text: DESIGNS PONY EXPRESS PAMPHLET. Mrs Neil Fitzpatrick received a pamphlet from her father, H. S. Hartley, last week. It was designed and drawn by him, commemorating the Pony Express ride now being rerun. The four paintings in it were purchased by the Western Tablet Co., of St. Joseph, Mo.

title: Third birthday: games with balloons
text: Birthday Party… Shawn Fitzpatrick celebrated his 3rd birthday anniversary by having a party, Saturday afternoon. His 15 guests spent the time playing games with balloons. Shawn received many nice gifts from his friends. Refreshments of birthday cake and jello were served.

title: Fourth birthday: Sheila plans the games
text: Birthday Party… Shawn Fitzpatrick was an honored guest at a birthday party at his home, Saturday afternoon when friends came to help him celebrate his 4th birthday anniversary. His sister, Sheila planned many interesting games for the afternoon’s entertainment. Favors of balloons were presented to the guests. Shawn then opened his gifts. Birthday cake and ice cream were served at the close of the party.

title: Sheila comes home by bus
text: Sheila Fitzpatrick returned home Thursday by bus from St. Joseph, Mo., where she visited for a few days with her grandparents, Mr. and Mrs. J. S. Hartley. Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick and Mrs. John Welch met her at Union.

title: Debbie Martin picks a president
text: …learned about the qualifications necessary to be able to vote. Each member of the class wrote a short item on “Why I would vote for (Mr Johnson or Mr Goldwater).” Debbie Martin writes “I think that if I were 21, I would vote for Mr Johnson. It is not fair to him. How would you feel, if you were President for only a few short months and someone like Mr Goldwater came along and took your place? Do you think that would be fair? So that’s why I want to vote for him.”

title: Hartley had art exhibit
text: Hartley Had Art Exhibit. Harrison Hartley, father of Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick of Weeping Water, exhibited 52 of his paintings at an art exhibit held at Hax Art Center, St. Joseph, Mo., from August 30 to Sept. 13. The exhibit was sponsored by the St. Joseph Art League. Mr. Hartley has worked as art director and artist for over 50 years at Des Moines, Ia., Kansas City, Mo., and St. Joseph. He has exhibited for the past 20 years at Nelson Gallery, Kansas City; Joslyn Memorial, Omaha; Art Gallery, Springfield, Mo.; Barn Gallery, St. Louis, Mo.; Arizona state fair; National Arts Club galleries, New York; Lever House, New York; 1939 New York world’s fair; and in one man shows in New York and St. Joseph.

title: Debby and Roddie arrive from California
text: HOME FROM CALIFORNIA. Mrs Art Fitzpatrick returned home Tuesday from an extended visit with her daughter, Mrs. Fred Martin and family at Redondo Beach, Calif. Debby and Roddie Martin returned home with Mrs Fitzpatrick for an indefinite visit with their grandparents.

title: Kindergarten: a class of 33
text: The 1964-65 kindergarten enrollment has now reached a total of 33. The names of the pupils and the name of the parent or guardian follows: Thomas E. Bauers, Robert Bauers; Cheryl Lynn Boydston, Cloyd Boydston; Karen Ann Brock, Dean Brock; Merle Lee Brockhoff, Ervin Brockhoff; David R. (Rusty) Dennis, David R. Dennis; Shawn Arthur Fitzpatrick, Neil Fitzpatrick; Kevin (Casey) Gwin, William Gwin; Diane Hanson, Beryl Hanson; Jerry Hollandsworth, Gerald Hollandsworth; Susan Marie Hunter, Dean Hunter; Michael D. Keckler, Richard Keckler…

title: First grade: spooks, goblins and cookies
text: In our Halloween Parade we had many wierd and ferocious looking spooks and goblins. We would like to thank Vernon Stander, Julie Irons, Fonda Mather, Casey Gwin, Mike Keckler, and Merle Brockhoff for bringing Halloween treats. We have had cookies with our milk recently, thanks to Rodney Seeger, Fonda Mather and Shawn Fitzpatrick.

title: Moved to Colorado
text: MOVED TO COLORADO. Mrs. Maryon Martin, Rodney and Debra left Wednesday to make their home at Arvada, Colo. They were accompanied by her mother, Mrs. Art Fitzpatrick and her brother, Neil Fitzpatrick.

title: Debbie Martin, news reporter
text: BROWNIE NEWS. Brownie troop met March 8, at the home of Mrs. Bob Baker. The Happy Birthday song was sung to Cami Parson, and Debby Martin. The Brownies played games and listened to records. Bonnie Cramer provided the treats. Debbie Martin, news reporter

title: Charles Fishpatrick
text: First day of summer arrived officially last Tuesday at 4:33 p.m. and since then we have had temperatures very much like summer… roses highlight the landscape, now rose ramblers at Roy Freemans, E. A. Michelsens, Grace Harters, rose borders at Hod Myers, Arnold Uptons… beautiful garden roses at Emily Olives, William Newhams, Charles Freemans… Robert Rathe reports that his Holstein cow gave birth to triplets on Sunday, June 26… Shawn Fitzpatrick has a new bug-eyed fish named Charles Fishpatrick…

title: Mary Fitzpatrick: hats off to the Alley Cat
text: Hats off to Larry and Lannie Hanson for giving the youth of our town somewhere to go in the afternoon and evenings. The Alley Cat is a place where youngsters from 12 to 20 are welcome to sit and talk, play their kind of music and just visit. Now if W.W. can get our swimming pool and tennis courts and keep our active recreation program our kids can call Weeping Water their town too! Mary Fitzpatrick

title: Seventh birthday
text: Birthday Party. Shawn Fitzpatrick was the guest of honor at a birthday party when eight children were invited to his home on Wednesday, Jan. 19, to help him celebrate his 7th birthday anniversary. After several games were played, Shawn opened his gifts. Cake and ice cream were served for this special occasion.

title: First Grade News
text: FIRST GRADE NEWS. We have been busily preparing our room for Valentine’s Day. We have a mailbox in which we mail our valentines. In science class we are now studying about the four seasons. We are learning about the weather and what we do in each season. In numbers we are adding and subtracting vertical problems. We just completed a section in our books on lines and line segments. We have had two birthdays in our room this past month. Fonda Mather and Shawn Fitzpatrick celebrated their seventh birthdays. Both brought cookies for everyone. We wish to thank Tommy Bauers, Rodney Seeger, and Diane Hanson for bringing cookies for our milk break. Mrs. Robert Bauers and Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick were recent visitors in our room.

title: Cub Scouts: in charge of the flag
text: …the Legion Hall Tuesday after school with their den mother, Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick. Shawn Fitzpatrick was in charge of the flag ceremony. The cubs worked on favors for the blue and gold banquet. Treats were provided by Shawn Fitzpatrick. Last Tuesday, Jan. 31 the cub scouts of den 1 went on a hike to the city lakes.

title: Mike Fitzpatrick wounded in Vietnam action
text: Mike Fitzpatrick Wounded in Vietnam Action. Mr. and Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick were notified yesterday that their son, L/Cpl. Michael N. Fitzpatrick, had been wounded in action, Wednesday, Oct. 11. Cpl Fitzpatrick was wounded by rifle fire in both legs while fighting with the 3rd Marine Division in the vicinity of Quang Tri, Vietnam. He is based on the carrier Okinawa, and has been returned to carrier for treatment. He had been in Vietnam just over a month. The Fitzpatricks were notified, both by a personal visit from a Marine sergeant, and a telegram they received last night. Mike’s condition is reported to be good.
warn: A family member wounded in action in Vietnam. The report says his condition was good.

title: Denis and Rex draw straws
text: In English we have written a letter to Susan Winters, an Omaha fourth grader, who wrote asking us about Weeping Water. Denis Fitzpatrick and Rex Boyd drew “Straws” to see which would copy our class letter in ink to send as they made the least mistakes in their letters. Rex drew “yes” so he copied the letter. Janet Harmon wrote her part about the bell in the carillon at First Plymouth Church…

title: Call from Australia
text: CALL FROM AUSTRALIA. Mr and Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick received a telephone call from their son, L/Cpl Michael Fitzpatrick who was on rest and recuperation leave from Vietnam in Australia. Enroute to Australia he stopped by for a visit with A/1C Jim Boardman, stationed at Da Nang.

title: A combat helmet and a boomerang
text: …Duff brought something green made of tissue paper. We called it a sea cucumber. Shawn Fitzpatrick brought his brother, Michael’s combat helmet for us to see and also a boomerang his brother had sent him.

title: Sunday in St. Joseph
text: Sunday Visit… Mr. and Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick, Mike, Brian, Shelia, Shawn and Dennis visited Sunday with Mr and Mrs. H. S. Hartley and Mrs. Helen Fortner at St. Joseph, Mo.

title: Count Down, Blast Off
text: FOURTH GRADE NEWS. Miss Kathryn Ellis teacher. “Count Down, Blast Off” and we are in orbit in the exciting realm of reading with “Take Off in Books” which is the title of our book project for November. Sue Wollen was the first astronaut to get her rocket in orbit. This she did by writing her book report, making her booklet cover, and her rocket. Cheryl Boydston was second in orbit followed by Michael Spohr, Renee Wessels, Shawn Fitzpatrick, Vicky Switzer, Dale Haveman, Patricia Scott, and Leslie Duff. Sue, Cheryl, and Michael are now in second orbit by next week and who knows, some may even go for third orbit or more. The more one reads the better reader he becomes and the more enjoyment he has in books.

title: Brian’s graduation at Milford
text: Attend Graduation. Mr and Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick, Shelia, Dennis and Shawn attended graduation exercises at the Nebraska Vocational Technical school at Milford last Thursday night, Dec. 5. Brian Fitzpatrick was one of the 160 graduates to receive a degree.

title: Second orbit
text: “Go Places in Books” was the slogan for Nat’l Book Week and most of us have been doing just that. We have 8 more astronauts in orbit. Merle Brockhoff, Dave Dennis, Michael Keckler, Kathryn Parson, Rodney Seeger, Patricia Sudman, Susan Hunter and Richard Wilson. Shawn Fitzpatrick and Vicky Switzer have completed their second orbit, Sue Wollen her third; and Cheryl Boydston, Michael Spohr and Renee Wessels their fifth orbit.

title: Which way is north?
text: While we were studying about all the ways to find which direction was north. Shawn Fitzpatrick and Julie Irons brought some tree bark with green lichens from the north side of a tree and Patricia Sudman some moss.

title: Mike on a one-man TV show
text: Around Town. March winds are in good form, blowing up dust, leaves, papers… everything but a much needed rain… Mike Fitzpatrick wrote to his parents telling about appearing on a 1 man TV show as he was entertained in an Australian home while on R & R from Vietnam.

title: Art exhibit: “Fun at the Pond”
text: In the art exhibit Michael Keckler won a 1st with his pencil drawing entitled, “A Sioux Camp,” Cheryl Boydston won 2nd with a pencil drawing of Indians “On the Move”, Patricia Scott, 2nd with a crayon design “Peacocks,” Shawn Fitzpatrick 3rd with a chalk picture “Fun at the Pond,” Cheryl Boydston 3rd with a charcoal “Mormons on the Trail” and Michael Keckler 3rd with a crayon “Cabin in the Woods.”

title: Book worms
text: Worms, anyone? We have a bulletin board teeming with them crawling along in green construction paper. Now they won’t be any good for “fishing for fish” but mighty good for “fishing for knowledge and fun.” They represent our reading books in leisure time when our lessons are finished. Each time we read a book we add a section to our worms. Cheryl Boydston and Renee Wessels have the longest worms with four sections; Shawn Fitzpatrick has three; Leslie Duff, Fonda Mather and Patricia Scott have two and Julie Irons, Kathryn Parson, Rodney Seeger, Michael Spohr, Vicky Switzer, William Norris, and Richard Wilson have one.

title: Softball throw: second place
text: Softball throw, 5 to 8, girls, Patty Scarlett, 1st; Cammy Colbert, 2nd; Brenda Franke, 3rd; boys, Chris Hansen, 1st; Bobby Hanes, 2nd; Roger Kuhn, 3rd; girls, 9 to 11, Sharon Clark, 1st; Sue Ann Wollen, 2nd; Denise Holt, 3rd; boys, John Fleming, 1st; Shawn Fitzpatrick, 2nd; Brent Brack, 3rd; girls, 12 to 14, Kathy Spencer, 1st; Karen Platt, 2nd; Patty Beck, 3rd; boys, Norman Clark, 1st; Dave Parson, 2nd; James West, 3rd.

title: Mike repairs the foundation
text: HERITAGE HOUSE NEWS. Work is progressing slowly. Mike Fitzpatrick as representative of the Jaycee’s undertook to repair the foundations of the old Dr. Fate office and has finished resetting the south side.

title: Heritage House needs help
text: Heritage House Needs Help! Work is proceeding slowly on the doctor’s office where Sam Baker has a fine set of steps and rails, as well as fixing the glass in the windows. Doctor Kunkel has been working on the interior walls and ceiling. Steve Guehlstorff has substituted for Pastor Campbell in pulling nails out of the paneled ceiling. Special paper and paint have been ordered; a new door (old style) has been put in the rear of the office and Doctor L N Kunkel has been fixing the screen windows. We still urgently need help in finishing scraping the exterior so that the whole building can be painted. So far this work has been done by Mike and Shawn Fitzpatrick, Mrs Ann Patterson and Susan, Tillie and Marilyn Miller, and Doctor Kunkel. There is much cleaning to be done and we need help for this.

title: Saturday at the Coopers
text: Mike, Dennis and Shawn Fitzpatrick visited Saturday at the Clifford Cooper home.

title: Arthur Fitzpatrick
text: Arthur Fitzpatrick Rites Held Aug. 9. Funeral services were held at the Congregational church, Thursday, August 9, 2:00 p.m., for Arthur R. Fitzpatrick who passed away Monday, August 6, 1973. Pastor I. C. G. Campbell officiated. Mrs. Raymond Freeman was organist. Pallbearers were Frank Wade, Roy T. Wade, Guy Hopkins, Roy Sterner, John Sterner and Robert Renner. Burial was at Oakwood Cemetery with Hobson-Dorr Funeral Home in charge of arrangements. OBITUARY. Arthur R. Fitzpatrick was born August 31, 1896 at Weeping Water, the son of Mr and Mrs. John Fitzpatrick. He married Violet I. Phillips, November 19, at Falls City. He worked for the Western Limestone Quarries at Weeping Water. He is survived by his wife Violet, 2 sons: Neil of Millard and James of Porterville, Calif.; two daughters Mrs. Earle (Gwen) Chamberlain of Ashland, Oregon, and Mrs. Maryon Martin of Arvada, Colo.; two sisters Mrs. Dean (Marie) Duncan and Mrs. Bonnie Trobough, both of Nebraska City; a brother, Wilbur of Louisville; 15 grandchildren and nine great-grandchildren. He was preceded in death by his parents, seven brothers and two sisters.

title: Carsten returned
text: CARSTEN RETURNED. In a non-political race the voters returned Senator Calvin Carsten, Avoca, to the State Legislature as their representative in the Second District. The soft-spoken Senator handily defeated Michael Neil Fitzpatrick who failed to carry one precinct. In Cass County, Senator Carsten was the winner 1770 to 990.

title: Mike files for the Legislature
text: MIKE FITZPATRICK FILES FOR STATE LEGISLATURE. Michael Neil Fitzpatrick of Weeping Water announced this week that he had filed for the office of member of the State Legislature, District 2, for a 4-year term. Fitzpatrick is the second person to announce his candidacy for this non-political office, as incumbent Calvin Carsten of Avoca had previously filed.

title: Marian Martin comes back
text: Moved to Weeping Water. Marian Martin of Arvada, Colo., has moved to Weeping Water and is making her home with her mother, Mrs. Art Fitzpatrick.

title: Home shingled
text: HOME SHINGLED. Mrs. Vi Fitzpatrick was surprised and delighted Sunday when members of her family arrived to shingle the roof of her home. Her son, Neil Fitzpatrick, and friend, Bill Denene of Omaha; grandsons, Shawn and Dennis of Omaha; Mike Fitzpatrick, Grand Forks, North Dakota; and Brian Fitzpatrick and Randy Beins and Mark Gwinn put new singles on and also cleaned up the yard. Mr. and Mrs. Mike Fitzpatrick and April came Saturday and were guests until Monday morning. Samantha, their other daughter, stayed with her grandparents, Mr. and Mrs. Ivan Rector. The Mike Fitzpatricks are moving back to this area. Vi Fitzpatrick served a picnic dinner for the workers.

title: Weekend visitors
text: Kit Cooper and Shawn Fitzpatrick were weekend visitors of Mr and Mrs. Clifford Cooper.

title: Shawn Fitzpatrick put up the sign
text: HONORED MONDAY—During the Chamber meeting and at a special open house was Margaret Boyd who retired December, 1988, after having worked at the City Library since 1973. Linville Prall pins a corsage on Mrs. Boyd at the Chamber dinner. Later in the afternoon, Mrs. Boyd was honored at the Community Center. She received a certificate of appreciation from Mayor Ed Gegg on behalf of the City of Weeping Water. Mrs. Boyd’s daughter JoAnn Boardman presented the Library Board with a clock and plaque in Mrs. Boyd’s name from her family. A new library sign has also been installed at the city library courtesy of Rex Boyd. Shawn Fitzpatrick put up the sign.

title: Violet Fitzpatrick
text: VIOLET FITZPATRICK. Born Jan. 5, 1901 in Bear Creek, Mo., Weeping Water resident Violet Fitzpatrick died Mon., March 18, 1991 at 90 years of age. Services were held Thurs., March 21 at the Methodist Church in Weeping Water. She married Arthur R. Fiztpatrick in 1920. She is survived by sons Arthur Neil of Omaha, James R. of Portersville, Calif.; daughter Gwen Chamberlain of Ashland, Ore.; 15 grandchildren, 20 great grandchildren and 3 great great grandchildren. She was preceded in death by her husband and daughter Maryon Martin. Pallbearers were Brian Fitzpatrick, Dennis Fitzpatrick, Shawn Fitzpatrick, Mike Lozier, Farley Amick, Stanley Miller. The family suggests memorials to the Weeping Water Rescue Squad. Arrangements were by Colbert Funeral Home of Weeping Water.

title: Brian’s bicycle accident
text: FRIDAY ACCIDENT. Brian Fitzpatrick, son of Mr. and Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick, was injured Friday when his bicycle hit a bump, throwing him to the pavement, striking the back of his head. He received a slight concussion and a few bruises and cuts; he was bedfast over the week end.
warn: A child's head injury from a bicycle fall.

title: Michael injures his left eye
text: INJURES LEFT EYE. Michael Fitzpatrick, son of Mr and Mrs Neil Fitzpatrick, fell and injured his left eye Monday and was taken to Dr Kunkel, and from there to Bryan Memorial hospital in Lincoln. Michael spent the night in the hospital and was able to come home Tuesday afternoon. No stitches had to be taken to close the wound in the white of the eye.
warn: A child's eye injury.

title: Eye doing nicely
text: EYE DOING NICELY. Mike Fitzpatrick, son of Mr. and Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick, is recovering nicely after the accident which injured his eye during the holidays. After a check with his doctor in Lincoln Friday, Mrs Fitzpatrick stated it is healing properly.
warn: A child's eye injury, recovering.

title: Sheila fractures a wrist
text: FRACTURES WRIST. Sheila Fitzpatrick, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick, fell down basement steps at her home Saturday evening, breaking both bones in her wrist. Her arm will be in a cast for several weeks.
warn: A child's broken wrist.

title: Break “no break” for Fitzpatricks
text: BREAK “NO BREAK” FOR FITZPATRICKS. On Tuesday, Neil Fitzpatrick broke two ribs while attempting to lift some heavy pipe while at work. He returned to work Wednesday morning. This is the second “break” in the Fitzpatrick family within the past two weeks. Shelia, small daughter of the Fitzpatricks, broke her arm the week before.
warn: Broken ribs and a child's broken arm.

title: Mary ill with near pneumonia
text: Mr and Mrs Harrison Hartley, St Joseph, Mo., spent the week end with their son-in-law and daughter, Mr and Mrs Neil Fitzpatrick and family, taking Denis Fitzpatrick home with them. Mrs Fitzpatrick was ill with near pneumonia. Visitors during her illness were Mrs Robert Renner, who cared for the children, Mrs Pat Wade, and Mrs Don Tieken. The Fitzpatricks plan to go to St Joseph for their son this coming Sunday.
warn: A serious illness in the family.

title: A kitchen fire
text: Mrs Neil Fitzpatrick reports that they had a narrow escape and an alarming experience last Sunday when the curtains and walls in the kitchen caught fire. Mrs Fitzpatrick was able to put out the fire without the help of the fire department, but still had considerable damage to the kitchen, besides the frightening moments.
warn: A house fire (no one was hurt).

title: Brian receives a head cut
text: RECEIVES HEAD CUT. Brian Fitzpatrick, 11-year-old son of Mr and Mrs Neil Fitzpatrick, met with an accident last Sunday when he slipped and fell, striking his head against a rock. The fall resulted in a severe head cut and several stitches were necessary to close the wound. Brian was alone when he fell, and ironically, was on a Boy Scout survival hike, and gave it a genuine test.
warn: A child's head wound.

title: 2-car crash Sunday evening
text: 2-Car Crash Sunday Evening. Mrs. Art Fitzpatrick is in critical condition in Bryan Memorial hospital, Lincoln, with injuries received in a 2-car accident at the intersection of state highways 50 and 1, Sunday evening about 5:30 p.m. Mrs. Fitzpatrick suffered a fractured collar bone, fractured toe, possible internal injuries, a back injury, and fractured ribs. Mr. Fitzpatrick was also taken to the hospital for treatment, but was released the same night. Bedford Harvey, who was riding in the Fitzpatrick car, apparently was uninjured. The Fitzpatrick car collided with a car driven by Richard Stratton, Lincoln, who with his parents, Mr. and Mrs. Russell Stratton, were returning to Weeping Water after visiting Glen Stratton at St. Joseph’s hospital in Omaha. The Fitzpatricks and Harvey were returning to Weeping Water from Manley, stopped at the stop sign at the intersection, then evidently pulled onto highway 50 in front of the southbound Stratton car. Mr. Fitzpatrick said that he did not see the other car, possibly because of the bright, setting sun. Russell Stratton received a cut on his chin which required seven stitches. Mrs. Stratton received severe bruises. Richard Stratton escaped injury. Both cars were virtually demolished.
warn: A car crash with serious injuries.

title: Vi returns home
text: Mrs. Art Fitzpatrick returned home Monday, May 2, from Bryan Memorial hospital where she was hospitalized for treatment of injuries received in an automobile accident.
warn: Recovery from a car crash.

title: Word from Vietnam
text: WORD FROM VIETNAM. Mr. and Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick received word from their son Michael Fitzpatrick who was recently wounded. He is making good progress and is walking with the aid of crutches. He has been temporarily transferred to the Phillipines. Mike wishes to express his appreciation and thanks to everyone for their cards, greetings, letters and get-well messages.
warn: A soldier recovering from wounds.

title: Neil’s thank-you
text: I wish to thank all who visited me and sent cards while I was in the hospital. Neil Fitzpatrick
warn: A hospital stay.

title: Neil’s motorcycle accident, recalled
text: From Our Files… One Year Ago… Sandi Baker represented Weeping Water as countess. Dr John Domingo arrived from Geneva, Switzerland for a visit with his mother. He was on leave from his work at Cern. Mrs. Don Walters and Devin left for England. Mr. and Mrs. John Norris returned from a 15 day tour in Alaska. Neil Fitzpatrick was injured in a motorcycle accident.
warn: A motorcycle accident.

title: Police court: no lights
text: Brian Fitzpatrick was charged with driving a motorcycle without lights. Pled guilty. Fined $7.00 and costs $4.00, total $11.00. Joe Bender, Police Judge. June 4, 1969.
warn: A court notice for a traffic offense.

title: A personal notice from Neil
text: PERSONAL NOTICE. I will not be responsible for debts incurred by anyone other than myself. Neil Fitzpatrick
warn: A public notice about debts.

title: Bake sale for Brian Fitzpatrick
text: BAKE SALE FOR BRIAN FITZPATRICK. A young man, born and raised in Weeping Water, has been sitting in a Mexican jail for a year awaiting trial. Brian Fitzpatrick, age 24, son of Mrs. Mary Fitzpatrick and Mr. Neil Fitzpatrick, both of Omaha. It has been reported that Brian has been severely beaten twice by at least ten commandos for leaving his cell without a shirt. Orders for the beatings were said to be given by a convicted murderer who is the cell-block “mayor.” Fitzpatrick was picked up for possession of one marijuana cigarette on January 19, 1974. A benefit bake sale will be given Saturday, Jan. 4. The money raised will be applied toward retaining an attorney for Brian.
warn: Imprisonment abroad and reports of beatings.

title: Bake sale nets $86
text: BAKE SALE NETS $86.00. Saturday’s “Bake Sale for Brian” netted $86.00. The sale was sponsored by several “Friends of Brian Fitzpatrick” who, hearing of the conditions under which he is awaiting trial in Mexico, decided to start a fund toward hiring a lawyer for him. At latest report, he has been in a Mexican jail awaiting trial for a year under extreme conditions. It is their hope a lawyer will expedite matters.
warn: Imprisonment abroad.

title: Languishing in a Mexico City jail
text: BRIAN FITZPATRICK, a 25-year-old Omahan who is a native of Weeping Water, languishes in a Mexico City jail. On Jan. 19, 1974, he was herded into Lecumberri prison with two Mexican-Americans. The three were charged with having two marijuana cigarets among them. Fitzpatrick’s mother learned last week her son’s trial was conducted July 28—more than 18 months after he was imprisoned—without her son being in court. An $8,000 fine was imposed or a three-year sentence in lieu of fine. The American Legion post at Weeping Water has arranged a Brian Fitzpatrick freedom fund for the honorably discharged Army veteran. The two Mexican-Americans were freed with lesser penalties. Fitzpatrick has been subjected to beatings, according to the mother, Mrs. Mary Fitzpatrick, 6312 No. 46th st., Omaha, a laid-off Vickers employe.

title: Hurt in cycle accident
text: Weeping Water Resident Hurt In Cycle Accident. Brian Fitzpatrick of Weeping Water was taken to a Lincoln hospital by the Weeping Water rescue squad Aug. 20 for treatment of injuries suffered when his motorcycle went out of control on the 13-J Spur in the early morning hours. Fitzpatrick had broken bones and possible internal injuries. His motorcycle was totaled. According to the Sheriff’s office, Fitzpatrick failed to negotiate a curve at about 3:30 a.m., causing him to leave the road, enter a ditch and strike a pole. The bike then rolled several times. The rider was not discovered until about 7:30 a.m. that day.

title: Preview: “it scares me”
text: After weathering two bad seasons in a row, Coach Jerry Park of Weeping Water is ready for a respectable one this year. More importantly, the Indians are also ready. A good part of this year’s squad started playing varsity ball when they were freshmen and sophomores, consequently, they have two or three seasons of experience under their belts. According to Park, this experience looks as though it will pay sizeable dividends this year. “The athletes are looking good in practice. They’re looking good all over, offensively and defensively. They look so good, in fact, it scares me,” says Park, who will need for his team to be very good indeed this weekend for their opener against top-ranked Nebraska City Lourdes. The Knights are rated as the team to beat in the Galaxy Conference this year. Park says his team should be capable of taking a good shot at the Nebraska City schoolboy grid power. “In spite of bad seasons the last two years, this team became convinced that they’re capable of being good ballplayers at the last game of the 1975 season when they defeated Louisville, 20-8. That win was the basis for a good attitude in pre-season practice this year,” said Park. Starters for Saturday night’s game are Mark Rupp, Chester Taylor, Pat Brim, Lloyd Philpot, Jeff Parson, Steve Mason, Mike Taylor and Doug Powell. Gene McKinstry and Rick Wilson will alternate. The other two starters were yet to be decided as of this past Tuesday. Parks says that offensively his team will primarily do their ground-gaining by running the ball. “We won’t pass too much this year. Defensively, the squad looks to be pretty solid, especially at the cornerback and linebacker positions.” Cornerbacks are Rick Wilson and Dave Schreiner. Chester Taylor and Steve Mason will hold down the linebacker positions. The Indians will play three away games (Lourdes, Sept. 4; Johnson-Brock, Sept. 10; and Elmwood, Sept. 17) before meeting Sterling at home Sept. 24. This will begin a four-week homestand with the following opponents to be Nemaha Valley,…

title: Lourdes 20, Indians 6
text: Indians “Scare” N.C. Lourdes Before Falling 20-6, Saturday. The Weeping Water Indians jumped to a 6-0 lead over the highly regarded Nebraska City Lourdes Knights Saturday night at Nebraska City, but were unable to maintain the lead and were defeated, 20-6. Lourdes was picked as the pre-season favorite to win the Class C-2 championship by the Omaha World-Herald. Indian fullback Chester Taylor blasted over from the three yard line to give the Indians their early lead but Joe Durr and Dick Wichman scored on 14 and 24 yard runs in the second period to put the Knights ahead at the half, 13-6. Weeping Water dominated the second half, driving to Lourdes’ five yard line twice only to be stalled by penalties both times. The Knights tallied the last score of the evening, later in the game, on a 52 yard run by Dave Schreiter. Two of NCL’s extra point attempts were good. Indian coach Jerry Park praised Taylor, who gained 79 yards on 11 carries, and the defensive performances of Rick Wilson and Jeff Parson. Park also pointed out that the whole offensive line did a commendable job. Park said, “Their (Lourdes’) superior team speed probably made the difference; however, we played well enough to win.” Weeping Water will play Johnson-Brock Friday, Sept. 10, at 7:30 p.m. Elmwood defeated Johnson-Brock last Friday, 22-6. text: Weeping Water’s Rick Wilson (No. 40 in white) rambles across the Nebraska City Lourdes’ 25 yard line in first quarter action last Saturday night. Other Weeping Water players pictured are Jeff Parson (74), Larry Culbertson (56), Lloyd Philpot (70), Chester Taylor (31), and Mark Rupp (83).

title: Indians 16, Johnson-Brock 12
text: Indians Come From Behind; Beat Johnson-Brock, 16-12. The Johnson Brock Eagles scored two first-quarter touchdowns Friday night to post an early 12-0 lead over the Weeping Water Indians. Eagle back Scott Brakhahn provided the first tally with a 65 yard run and the Indians supplied the opportunity for J-B’s second TD with a fumble on their own 35 yard line. Dale Piper ran for the 20 yard score and the 12-0 lead. The Indians settled down in the second period and drove 60 yards for a score. Quarterback Dave Schreiner went the last three yards and also ran the two point conversion for a 12-8 score. In the closing minutes of the half, Schreiner again scored, from the six this time, and added the conversion run to account for all of the Indians’ 16 points in the 16-12 victory. Steve Mason aided Schreiner’s second TD run with a fine block. After allowing Johnson-Brock 108 first quarter rushing yards, the Indian defense surrendered only 102 yards throughout the remainder of the game. Offensively, Rick Wilson rushed 20 times for 103 yards, a personal high, and Chester Taylor carried 17 times for 67 yards. Schreiner added 47 yards on seven carries. The Indians passed only three times, completing two for 15 yards. Bruce Sorensen and Mark Rupp were on the receiving end of Schreiner’s passes. Defensively, Doug Powell replaced Schreiner in the secondary and played an excellent game as did Wilson. Schreiner suffered an ankle injury in the Nebraska City Lourdes game and was limited to offensive duty against J-B. Linebacker Mike Keckler turned in several good plays during the night, as did defensive linemen John Bauers and Lloyd Philpot. Regular safety Gene McKinstry missed the game with a sprained ankle. Indian coach Jerry Park said that he felt the Indians played with a lack of enthusiasm in the first quarter, possibly because they had been so emotionally high for the previous week’s Nebraska City Lourdes contest. Park pointed out that the Indians played a good game after they fell behind, 12-0. The Indians will play at Elmwood Friday, Sept. 17, at 7:30 p.m. Elmwood defeated Johnson-Brock two weeks ago, 22-6. Score by quarters: Weeping Water 0 8 8 0—16. Johnson-Brock 12 0 0 0—12.

title: Indians 20, Elmwood 14
text: Indians Over Elmwood, 20-14; Season Record Is 2-1. The Weeping Water Indians, led on offense by the running of Chester Taylor, raised their season record to 2-1 last Friday night with a 20-14 win over the Elmwood Pirates. Taylor gained 171 yards in 23 attempts. The Indians have rushed for more than 200 yards in each of their three games. Elmwood nearly scored on the first offensive series of the game, marching to the Indian five yard line only to be held there by the Indian defense. In the second period, Weeping Water moved 60 yards for a score with quarterback Dave Schreiner gaining 46 of the yards on two carries. Brent Brack scored the TD on a three yard run and Schreiner added the two point conversion. Schreiner reinjured an ankle on that run and was replaced by sophomore Jim Wipf. Taylor notched Weeping Water’s second score in the third period, going over from the one yard line. The conversion attempt failed and the Indians led, 14-0. Elmwood cut the lead to 14-6 in the last period on a one yard run by quarterback Chris Hansen. The extra point attempt failed. Larry Culbertson. Defensive players singled out by Park as outstanding were Taylor, Philpot, guard Don Colbert and defensive backs Rick Wilson and Gene McKinstry. Weeping Water will meet Sterling in their annual Homecoming game Friday night at 7:30 p.m. Game statistics: First downs WW 10, Elm 9. Yds rushing 258, 72. Yds passing 71, 99. Total yds 329, 171. Weeping Water 0 8 6 6—20. Elmwood 0 0 0 14—14.

Greg Vogt scored the conversion to make the final score 20-14. title: Indians 16, Sterling 8: Homecoming
text: Indians Defeat Sterling In Homecoming Contest. The Weeping Water Indians scored 16 second quarter points and overcame nine offensive turnovers to defeat the Sterling Jets, 16-8, here in the Bicentennial Homecoming football contest Friday night. The Indians led, 16-0, until a fumble on their seven yard line late in the game allowed Sterling to score. Rick Wilson led the offensive thrust with 140 yards rushing in only 13 attempts for a 10.8 yard average per carry. Gene McKinstry averaged a whopping 13.2 yards per carry, gaining 66 yards on five rushes. McKinstry’s average was helped by a 45 yard touchdown sprint for the Indians’ second score. Chester Taylor gained 65 yards on 14 attempts. Overall, the Indians rushed for 279 yards behind fine blocking supplied by the offensive line. The Indian defense held Sterling to only 123 total yards, 56 rushing and 67 passing. Weeping Water’s first score came on a 24-yard touchdown pass from Jeff Parson to Morgan Whale in the second period. Wilson added the two point conversion run. McKinstry’s 45 yard run also came in the second period. Jim Wipf passed to Bruce Sorensen for the conversion. The Jets’ score and conversion were on pass plays from Kim VanGonigan to Don Schuster. Indian Coach Jerry Park indicated that aside from the turnovers (six fumbles and three pass interceptions), he felt that the team played well. He cited the offensive blocking of Jeff Parson and Steve Mason as a key factor in the rushing attack and praised the complete defensive unit for shutting down Sterling’s excellent passing attack. The defense dropped the Sterling quarterback for losses five times on passing attempts. Parents’ Night. The Indians, now 3-1, will play at home against Nemaha Valley Friday night at 7:30 p.m. in the annual Parents’ Night game. Parents of squad members will be introduced at halftime.

title: Indians 28, Nemaha Valley 14
text: Indians Chalk Up Fourth Win, 28-14. The Weeping Water Indians football team defeated Nemaha Valley last Friday to give them their fourth win of the season after losing their first game to Nebraska City Lourdes. Weeping Water scored first, but Nemaha Valley came right back to tie it up in the first quarter, 6 to 6. In the second quarter, both teams scored again, and at half-time the score was 14 to 14. The third quarter was scoreless, but in the fourth quarter, the Indians came alive and scored 14 more points while holding Nemaha Valley scoreless. The game ended with Weeping Water winning, 28 to 14. Dave Schreiner was high scorer for Weeping Water with 18 points, followed by Rick Wilson with 8 points and Bruce Sorensen with 2 points. Weeping Water’s leading rusher was Rick Wilson with 146 yards, followed by Dave Schreiner with 98 yards and Chester Taylor with 76 yards. Weeping Water had a total offense of 350 yards while Nemaha Valley had a total offense of 242 yards. Weeping Water now has a won 4, lost record of 4 wins and 1 loss. Their next game is tomorrow night against Stella S.E.

title: Stella Southeast 12, Indians 6
text: Indians Lose To Stella; Face Mt. Michael Friday. A nine-man defensive front used by Stella Southeast held the usually potent Weeping Water High rushing attack to 133 yards Friday night as the Indians lost, 12-6. The Indians were averaging nearly 250 yards rushing per game going into the Stella contest. The first three quarters of the game were scoreless, with both teams performing well defensively, but Stella scored on a 60 yard pass play and a six yard run in the final period before the Indians could get on the scoreboard with a 25 yard run by Rick Wilson. The Indians’ attempt to regain possession of the ball after their score on an onside kick failed. The Indian effort received two setbacks early in the contest when backs Dave Schreiner and Jeff Parson were lost for the night with injuries. Chester Taylor, Wilson and Gene McKinstry rushed for 49, 44 and 29 yards, respectively, for the Indians and Jim Wipf was 3 for 10 in the passing department for 30 yards. Mark Rupp caught one of those passes for 25 yards. The Indians, now 4-2 for the season, face Elkhorn Mt. Michael in Weeping Water Friday night at 7:30 p.m.

title: Mount Michael 32, Indians 26
text: Indians Lose To Elkhorn Mt. Michael For Third Loss Of Season. Elkhorn Mount Michael defeated Weeping Water last Friday night to give the Indians their third loss of the year. The final score was 32 to 26. Rick Wilson scored the first touchdown of the game, putting Weeping Water ahead, 6 to 0. When Weeping Water kicked off, Mount Michael ran it all the way back for a touchdown. They made the 2 point conversion, and Mount Michael went ahead, 8 to 6. Later, Dan Manley threw a pass to Bruce Sorenson for a touchdown. Weeping Water’s try for the extra point was good, and Weeping Water was ahead again, 14-8. Weeping Water’s lead did not last long, because Mount Michael scored again in 5 plays, and tied it up, 14 to 14. Dave Schreiner scored another touchdown for Weeping Water, putting Weeping Water ahead 20 to 14 at half-time. In the third quarter, each team scored one touchdown, and at the end of the third quarter, Weeping Water was still ahead, 26 to 20. In the fourth quarter, Mount Michael scored 12 points while holding Weeping Water scoreless, and Mount Michael won, 32 to 26. Dave Schreiner was Weeping Water’s leading scorer with 12 points, followed by Rick Wilson with 8 points. Dave Schreiner was also Weeping Water’s leading rusher, with a total of 130 yards. [A second item follows, on the Stella game:] Weeping Water’s football team was defeated by Stella S.E. last Friday to give Weeping Water their second loss of the season. Neither team scored in the first three quarters. In the fourth quarter, Stella scored two touchdowns before Weeping Water finally managed to get on the board. The final score was 12 to 6. Stella’s first touchdown drive…

title: Palmyra 40, Indians 8
text: Palmyra Defeats Indians, 40-8. Weeping Water’s football team was defeated by Palmyra last Friday night, 40 to 8. Palmyra scored the only touchdown in the first quarter. Their touchdown came from a 9 yard drive after Weeping Water fumbled on their own 9 yard line. In the second quarter, Weeping Water scored their only touchdown of the game. The Indians drove 48 yards, and the touchdown was made by Chester Taylor. The points after touchdown were made by Rick Wilson. Palmyra also scored one touchdown in the second quarter. In the third quarter, Palmyra scored 25 points, while holding Weeping Water scoreless. In the fourth quarter, neither team scored, and the game ended with the score 40 to 8. Weeping Water’s leading rusher was Rick Wilson with 59 yards, followed by Brent Brack with 32 yards. The Indians’ last game of the season was played Wednesday night against Louisville. title: Louisville 41, Indians 14
text: Lions Defeat Weeping Water. The Louisville Lions, paced by Kirk Cundall’s four touchdowns, romped to a 41-14 victory over the Weeping Water Indians last Wednesday night in Weeping Water. The gridiron match marked the end of the season for both teams. The contest was close throughout the first half, as Louisville went to the locker room with a 21-14 lead. But the Lions exploded in the second half, scoring 13 points in the third quarter and seven more in the fourth, while the defense throttled the Indian offensive attack. Weeping Water broke out to a 6-0 lead, with fullback Chester Taylor scoring from one yard out at 4:24 of the first period. The Lions came back to take the lead with 1:16 remaining in the opening quarter, as Cundall scored his first touchdown on a four yard run. Mike Maher’s extra point gave Louisville a 7-6 edge. Rick Wilson broke loose for a 27 yard touchdown run early in the second quarter, and Quarterback Dave Schreiner ran for the two-point conversion to give Weeping Water a 14-7 advantage. But the Lions roared back down the field, as several big plays advanced the ball to the three yard line. Brian Sparks scored from there, and added the two-point conversion to put Louisville out in front for good, 15-14, at 8:16 of the second quarter. This score seemed to breathe new life into the Louisville defense, as they repeatedly turned back scoring threats by the Indian offensive unit. Cundall blasted over from one yard out with a half a minute remaining in the half, and the Lions led at halftime, 21-14. The second half was all Louisville, as the Lions marched to three touchdowns while shutting Weeping Water out. Cundall scored twice in the third quarter; first on a 16 yard run with 7:00 left in the period, and again with 1:25 remaining on a run of 17 yards. Maher kicked the extra point following Cundall’s final touchdown, and then scored himself on a four yard run at 3:29 of the fourth quarter. The Indians rushing was led by Gene McKinstry and Chester Taylor with 77 yards each. Rick Wilson had 71 yards, followed by Dave Schreiner with 51 yards and Mike Keckler with seven yards. The Indians’ record for the season is 4-5.

title: The all-conference team
text: The All Conference Team. Defensive halfback Rick Wilson, defensive tackle Lloyd Philpot and offensive guard Steve Mason were the Weeping Water Indians named to the Galaxy North Division All Conference football team this week. Wilson, a senior, was selected for all conference honors for the second time. According to Indian Coach Jerry Park, “Rick is a good defensive back, particularly against the run. He comes up from his defensive position very well to stop ball carriers.” Park said that defensive tackle Lloyd Philpot, a senior, is “very consistent, a hard worker and had no bad ball games.” Offensive guard Steve Mason, a junior, “led our offensive line and is a fine blocker,” according to Park. Indians selected for honorable mention all conference were fullback Chester Taylor, quarterback Dave Schreiner and tackle Jeff Parson. Wilson was also honorable mention, as an offensive back. The fact that three offensive backs were selected as honorable mention was a tribute to the whole Indian offensive unit. The team averaged almost 250 yards rushing per game for the season.
